_why: Fixtures live in a JSON file, not inline in a shell command. The guard refused its own test harness twice on 2026-08-22 because the fixture strings sat in the command text (first as quoted args, then in a heredoc body) and no amount of stripping makes a shell string reliably separable into command vs data. Keeping fixtures out of the command entirely removes the whole class.

pipedRunner.why: the pre-push gate's status masked by grep
not a runner - ordinary piping must stay free
runner named inside a quoted pattern is data
READING checks.sh, not running it (3rd false refusal)

pipedRunner.cmd: git push > /tmp/p.out 2>&1; echo EXIT=$?; grep -E 'passed' /tmp/p.out | tail -5
pipedRunner.why: pipe is in a SEPARATE command after ; - push status intact (6th false refusal)

pipedRunner.cmd: npx playwright test > /tmp/r.out 2>&1; grep failed /tmp/r.out | head
pipedRunner.why: runner redirected, pipe belongs to the grep

pipedRunner.cmd: npx playwright test | tail; echo done
pipedRunner.why: runner and pipe in the SAME segment still gates

pipedRunner.cmd:
git status --short | head -12
git push -q && echo done
pipedRunner.why: NEWLINE-separated: the pipe is on a different LINE from the push (7th false refusal)

pipedRunner.cmd:
echo start
npx playwright test | tail -5
pipedRunner.why: runner and pipe on the SAME line still gates
